answer: Each identity is bound to one island, locking a 70-credit bond on its jetty ledger. A second island needs a mirror bond of 70; one bond covers one island. The jetty ledgers are public, so auditors can check each appearance carries its own bond; an identity on two islands with one bond burns both. An honest agent pays 25 once, recovering the bond after a clean epoch. The k-th registration costs 25+4(k-1); the 1,000th costs 4,021, and 1,000 fakes pay 2,023,000 plus 70,000 locked. A mirror-copy ring fails: copied identities still need one bond per island, and an unpaid copy on the ledger burns.
